essential: Peter Chardon Brooks's death and estate. Henry was the fourth child, 'being of less account,' named for his mother's brother.
The brothers-in-law Everett, Frothingham, and Adams, distinguished and unlike. Cousins sleep through sermons as inheritors of feuds.

Why C. F. Adams did not take State Street's succession: J. Q. Adams's record and the slave-power. The children were anti-slavery by birth. Keep the image of Webster as archangel with the flaming sword.

1848 as an indelible stamp like 1776, with C. F. Adams as Free Soil vice-presidential nominee. The Puritan resists change, believing his standards higher; 'So they were.' Henry by nature would have gone into the Church.
Pilotage: the father's channel was clear, the sons faced an unknown ocean. The 1840–1870 generation could use old education; that of 1870–1900 needed something new.

The father's poise in detail: no snobbery, flattery, or vanity; mental faculties not exceptional, but 'Within its range it was a model.' He was called cold, yet he chose a middle path between Webster's party and Garrison's secession and 'set up a party of his own.' He stood alone, with no master and no scholars.
The Mount Vernon Street circle: Palfrey, light and worldly; Dana, refinement hardened to labor; Sumner, solitary, Anglophile, ostracized, his solitude 'glacial.' Henry worshipped Sumner as 'heroic.'
The writing-table in the library, the Latin Grammar, proof-correcting John Adams's Works, and the punctuation joke. Everything he absorbed was of the past.
New England government by the professions and 'by the best,' the Webster succession, and the European middle-class parallel. No one except Marx foresaw change.

Unitarian calm and the puzzle of the vanished religion. The children threw off church at the first moment. He calls this the most curious phenomenon of his life, a society 'turning away one's eyes as one approaches a chasm.' Note Emerson's 'naif' protest.

Literary and political table-talk: Louisa, John, the father reading Hosea Biglow. He declined Wordsworth until he was thirty. The family was one type with half-a-dozen facets, all wanting 'to control power in some form.'

Hatred of school as a 'positive gain,' slow memory, school-days reckoned as waste, the four tools he never controlled. Boston amusements taught nothing; he learned most lying on Congressional Documents at Quincy reading Scott.
optional: The full list of Brooks children by name.
Detailed Everett career, keeping only that he left the pulpit for Congress and was second to Webster.
Dana's 'woolsack' ambitions and the Evarts quotation; cut both together.
The Peter Harvey cheques and the Winthrop succession detail.
The 'Were half the power' quatrain (para 18). It can go if the sentence introducing it is reworded so it does not end on a colon.
The sports catalogue in para 27, reduced to 'no sport worth learning.'
The 'ant or an elephant' joke; keep its premise with it or cut both.
risks: The chapter is dense with abstract argument. Over-compressing the father/poise passage risks losing the hedged 'No doubt...' qualifications.

title: BOSTON (1848-1854)

verbatim.purpose: States the inherited bias as a fixed warp.
verbatim.text: even when only ten years old, his face was already fixed, and his heart was stone, against State Street; his education was warped beyond recovery in the direction of Puritan politics.

verbatim.purpose: Central judgment of the father, later tested in London.
verbatim.text: Charles Francis Adams possessed the only perfectly balanced mind that ever existed in the name.

verbatim.purpose: Aphoristic explanation of why the father was called cold.
verbatim.text: The world never loved perfect poise. What the world does love is commonly absence of poise, for it has to be amused.

verbatim.purpose: Fixes the hero-worship that later breaks.
verbatim.text: Sumner was the boy's ideal of greatness; the highest product of nature and art.

verbatim.purpose: Signature ironic hyperbole about a misleading education.
verbatim.text: All experience since the creation of man, all divine revelation or human science, conspired to deceive and betray a twelve-year-old boy who took for granted that his ideas, which were alone respectable, would be alone respected.
Boston had solved the universe; or had offered and realized the best solution yet tried. The problem was worked out.
He thought his mind a good enough machine, if it were given time to act, but it acted wrong if hurried. Schoolmasters never gave time.

verbatim.purpose: The four tools are a recurring measure of his deficiency.
verbatim.text: the facile use of only four tools: Mathematics, French, German, and Spanish.

voice_profile: Third-person autobiography in which the aged author calls his younger self 'he,' 'the boy,' or 'Henry Adams.' It moves between the child's limited view and the old man's retrospective irony. It relies on aphorism and paradox, such as 'Summer was the multiplicity of nature; winter was school.' Self-deprecation is played as mock-scientific analysis: variation, type, force, stamp. Long periodic sentences end in a dry reversal. Lists build through dashes and semicolons. Exact dates anchor the account. Qualifiers like 'perhaps,' 'probably,' and 'he could never decide' recur. Every episode is measured as a lesson in education that taught little or the wrong thing. Double hyphens are characteristic and must be kept.
